findings.body:
**Reject tag object IDs passed as `--sha`.**

At `prepare-host.py`, Line 790, the check accepts any 40-character lowercase hex string. Without `--tag`, the object ID of an annotated tag can pass: Git peels it for the ancestry and tree checks, and checkout detaches at the underlying commit. The intent record and `switch()` return value still identify the tag object, not the commit at HEAD. Require `git cat-file -t` to report `commit` before checking ancestry. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/v2.43.0/builtin/merge-base.c))
findings.title: Reject tag object IDs passed as `--sha`.

findings.body:
**Include the initial config restore in switch recovery.**

At `prepare-host.py`, Line 834, `git restore` runs before the recovery block. If a post-checkout hook fails after Git writes the file, HEAD stays at the prior commit but the host overrides are gone. The next switch fails the drift check. Git can report the hook failure after updating the file. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/v2.43.0/builtin/checkout.c))

Start recovery before the first restore. If the failure occurs before checkout, reinstall the saved rendering without repeating the failed restore. Keep the existing checkout rollback for failures after HEAD moves.
findings.title: Include the initial config restore in switch recovery.

findings.body:
**Read launchd templates from the same commit as the preview config.**

At `prepare-host.py`, Lines 728–729, `render_plists()` reads the worktree. If a local edit changes a plist's `ProgramArguments`, preview exports the edit while rendering the config and systemd units from committed sources. The preview no longer represents the checked-out commit.

Resolve one commit under the preview lock. Use it to list and read the launchd templates as well as the config and systemd templates.
findings.title: Read launchd templates from the same commit as the preview config.

findings.body:
**Emit a JSON artifact on operation failure without `--json`.**

At `prepare-host.py`, Line 996, only machine mode gets an error artifact. For example, `live-config` with a missing overlay exits 1 and leaves stdout empty unless the caller passes `--json`.

Emit the error artifact in both modes. Keep stderr narration conditional so `--json` still produces no stderr. As per coding guidelines, “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout and human narration to stderr, never mixed.”
findings.title: Emit a JSON artifact on operation failure without `--json`.

findings.body:
**Refuse unit destinations that would replace the overlay.**

At `prepare-host.py`, Line 771, `prepare` can overwrite its input overlay. If the private overlay is named `crq-tick.service` and lives in `--units-output`, the stale-file check accepts it because that name is in the rendered set. The install then replaces the overlay, and the next invocation cannot load it.

Pass the overlay path into the installation preflight. Reject a matching destination before writing the intent record or any units.
findings.title: Refuse unit destinations that would replace the overlay.

findings.body:
**Validate switch arguments before loading the helper.**

In machine mode, `switch --unit crq-tick.service` without `--runtime` loads the helper and then emits `kind: "refused"`. This is an argument error. Validate both switch modes before loading the helper and send invalid combinations through `parser.error` so the response names `switch` and exits 2 with `kind: "usage"`.

As per coding guidelines, doctrine I1 says that in machine mode an argument error with no result writes one JSON object with `"kind": "usage"` and `"exitCode": 2`.
findings.title: Validate switch arguments before loading the helper.

findings.body:
**Record the helper digest in unit transaction journals.**

The unit switch loads the helper to read the overlay, but the journal identity omits `helper_sha256`. Pending, completed, and rolled-back unit records therefore cannot identify the helper bytes used, contrary to Lines 28–29. Pass `helper_sha256` into `switch_unit` and retain it in the transaction identity. Recovery should preserve that original digest.
findings.title: Record the helper digest in unit transaction journals.

findings.body:
**Check recovery against the queue state observed under the new fence.**

If a switch fails in `drained` and its first rollback also fails, another issuing unit can complete a tick before the next `recover`. The next recovery passes the fresh drain and restores the snapshot, but preservation still compares the current queue and heartbeat with the old transaction digests. The check fails even if restore changed neither file. Repeating `recover` uses the same stale baseline.

Capture the preservation baseline after the new fence and before restore. Retain the original digests separately so the journal still shows what changed between attempts.
findings.title: Check recovery against the queue state observed under the new fence.

findings.body:
**Match rollback to the current deployment transaction, not just HEAD.**

After completed deployments A → B → C → B, both journals that deployed B pass the HEAD check. Passing the first journal can switch the host to A even though the current deployment's predecessor is C.

Validate the supplied journal against the active completed checkout transaction under the controller lock. Refuse a superseded journal even if its target SHA matches HEAD.
findings.title: Match rollback to the current deployment transaction, not just HEAD.

findings.body:
**Do not start rollback while the journal can still say `completed`.**

`journal_replace` replaces the record before it syncs the directory. If the directory sync fails, the new `completed` record can already be visible. The exception handler then stops or restores the unit. If the process exits before it writes the rollback phase, the next invocation accepts `completed` and proceeds despite the interrupted rollback. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/os.html?utm_source=openai))

Distinguish failures before replacement from failures after replacement. If completion is already visible but its durability is uncertain, report that uncertainty and leave the activated unit intact. Start rollback only after an unfinished record is durable again.
findings.title: Do not start rollback while the journal can still say `completed`.

findings.body:
**Use one journal directory for all transactions on the checkout.**

If a checkout switch leaves a pending record in directory A, a second invocation can pass directory B with the same `--root` and `--overlay`. The controller takes the same lock, but `refuse_unfinished_transactions` scans only B. The pending record in A no longer prevents a mutation.

Bind the journal directory to the validated checkout configuration. If `--record-dir` remains an option, require it to match that directory before any mutation.
findings.title: Use one journal directory for all transactions on the checkout.

findings.body:
**The rollback compatibility check can go stale before checkout mutation.**

`rollback_plan` runs the drain and compatibility checks at `deploy-controller.py:2280-2295`, then captures state and calls `helper_module.switch` at line 2303. The controller does not take `tick.lock` itself on this path. `prepare-host.py` `switch` takes `tick_lock(root)` at line 825 and re-runs `inactive(root)` at line 826, but it does not re-run any queue compatibility check. A supported runner entrypoint that starts after the drain and writes `author_*` state before line 825 can therefore reach checkout with a queue the prior target cannot read. The concern is confined to that window; the unit-inactivity recheck under the lock does not cover it.

Whether such an entrypoint can run while the units are stopped is not established by the inspected source. The docstring at `deploy-controller.py:385-386` says tick, slot, and repair passes take the same flock. The runner's unit-based dispatch is blocked by `inactive`, but a manual invocation path was not inspected.

Suggested change: re-run `compatibility_record` and the `rollback_compatible` check under the tick lock, or hold the lock from the drain through the switch.
findings.title: The rollback compatibility check can go stale before checkout mutation.
